I'm good with computers but have no idea what type of positions exist and what's required to do them. Where can I get some helpful info on where to start? Any help is appreciated, thanks!
I want to start a new career
Get certifications. They are huge in the technology job market today.

Which certifications are good to get for someone interested in programming or web development? I've been looking into certifications, but it seems like some require professional experience in the field.

Honestly, none. There are no industry standard certifications for programming or web development. A body of work is more effective than a certification of dubious quality. In other words, make a github account and start uploading your projects.

That depends on what you like to do and are good at. Do you like setting up workstations and laptops? Help desk may be for you? Installing and setting up servers? System admin. Writing software? Programmer. Testing software for bugs? QA. Hacking? Penetration tester. Give us some hints about your skills and desires.
Well that was kind of my point when I said I wasn't sure what positions existed lol from your examples, I'd say help desk.

What is your current career? If you just want to do a job that you don't have to worry too much about then help desk/tech support is probably right for you and quite easy to get into in certain locations.

If you want to be a programmer, then some things to take into consideration. For a lot of people; there is the code you want to write and the code you have to write. I personally love all the projects I work on, but for some it can make the job tedious. The challenge of pushing your boundaries and solving problems is a lot of fun though.

QA work and perma-debugging is a little unpredictable and transient at least from companies I've worked with.

The field is really wide open. If you like programming, that is a great field. You can specialize in increasingly granular areas too, like creating beautiful UIs, or doing back end services. Maybe get super specific and specialize in optimizing the windows kernel.

If you like the configuration aspects or hardware, you may be more of an IT person. They do everything from restart computers for salespeople to setting your company's VPN so you can securely access your data center. Good IT people are a godsend.

No matter what, start by taking introductory courses at a community college. Talk to the teachers about your interests and they will help you focus your studies.

But basically, if you are good with computers, there are jobs waiting for you (with proper study). If you are also pleasant to work with, people will throw money at you.
